# Identification Phase 4: internal flows on the generation kit

**Generated by `npm run idphase4` from `scripts/build-identification-phase4.mjs`. Do not edit by hand.**

[IDENTIFICATION_SYSTEM.md](../../../reference/identification/IDENTIFICATION_SYSTEM.md) §13, Phase 4. Each file is the
flow's root scope as the tenant capture holds it (`docs/folio-Master-Flows-and-Endpoints/captures/`), with the edits
below applied. `tests/identification-phase4.test.mjs` runs every file in the strict simulator and checks the designer's
limits (nesting depth 8, no variable declared inside a pasted scope).

## Before pasting

Phases 1 to 3 as recorded in [identification-phase1](../identification-phase1/README.md),
[identification-phase2](../identification-phase2/README.md) and [identification-phase3](../identification-phase3/README.md).
The first TASK claim of a year creates the counter row `TASK-<year>` in Portal Sequence Counters; nothing has to be
created by hand.

## Caller identity (G-04)

Every internal endpoint key resolves its caller the same way (SINGLE_ASSIGNMENT, BULK_ASSIGNMENT, FETCH_ALL, DYNAMIC_ACTIONS
and SUBSIDIARY_ACTIONS, EMAIL_RELATED_TASK, REFERENCE_DATA, GET_DOCS and FETCH_ACTIVITIES, FETCH_EMAIL_ATTACHMENTS, EMAIL and
the three AI keys), through one Flow Configuration switch, `IDENTITY_PROOF_REQUIRED`:

| Switch | Caller | Refused |
|---|---|---|
| not `true` (no row, or any other value) | the sign-in proof's address when a valid proof is sent, else the address the request names (`userEmail`; Bulk also `requestedBy`) | as before these packages: FETCH_ALL, DYNAMIC_ACTIONS and EMAIL by their own directory and role gate; the others not at all (REFERENCE_DATA and GET_DOCS had a gate whose decision was hard-coded to pass) |
| `true` | only the sign-in proof's address: the bearer token Folio sends, found in the proof ledger unconsumed, Purpose internal-session and unexpired | no valid proof, or not an active directory user: 401. A role without the endpoint's route (single-assignment, bulk-assignment; `"*"` and `bulk:assign` also pass): 403 |

This is the enforcement of [G-04](../../../deployment/PRODUCTION_READINESS_REGISTER.json), carried by the identification
packages so that applying it is setting the switch, not pasting other flows over these. The proof is minted by IP_OTP_VERIFY
(`OTP_VERIFY__IP_OTP_VERIFY__4dbe6dde.paste.json`, below). Set the switch only after that package is pasted and Folio
users can sign in: before then no client holds a valid proof and every call would be refused. The DGO_* replacement
packages that carried an earlier form of this are retired (2026-10-06, registers/flow-retirement.json).

REFERENCE_DATA and GET_DOCS do not yet enforce a role's route or permission, only the caller: which roles hold them is not
recorded in this repository. REFERENCE_DATA serves the full directory (Role, Persona, Status, AccessScope, PilotCohort) only
to a holder of `user:view` or `"*"`, and to anyone else on the caller's own row.

The directory row's `Role` is a Choice column (docs/reference/sharepoint-provisioning-spec.json). FETCH_ALL and
DYNAMIC_ACTIONS read it as text, which never matched a `RoleId`; every package here reads its value.

## One bulk assignment endpoint

Folio calls one bulk endpoint, `BULK_ASSIGNMENT` (modules/bulk-assignment.js). Its URL is the trigger of
BULK_OPS_DATA_RETRIEVAL_HTTP (`5aab9e61`), which only read documents, so a bulk assignment created no task. That flow
now holds the bulk assignment scope below and is the one bulk endpoint kept. `BULK_ASSIGNMENT_DIRECT`
(IP_Bulk_Assign_Endpoint, `0d1e8df5`, reassignment only) is called by nothing in Folio and is retired: turn that flow
off, and leave its URL out of the endpoint configuration. The legacy Deployed Bulk Task Assignment_Create Task
(`122bb363`) is not wired to Folio and stays off.

## Changes

### Single_Task_Assignment

- S8 / ID-19: every run mints its Request ID. varRequestId was declared with no value and never set, so every reply and error record carried an empty requestId. The root scope now sets it to guid() first.
- G-04: the caller is resolved as every identification package resolves it (see "Caller identity" above): from the sign-in proof when one is valid; else, while IDENTITY_PROOF_REQUIRED is not true, from userEmail as today. With the switch true, a caller who is not an active directory user is refused with 401 and one whose role does not allow single-assignment (or bulk:assign) with 403, through the flow's own validation-failure path, before any task is claimed or written. The task's AssignedBy is that caller.
- ID-19: the reply's requestId is always the flow's own. It took the client's requestId whenever the request carried one.
- S3 / §8.2: each new task gets a Task Reference TASK-YYYY-NNNNN, claimed by the generation kit (10 flat attempts, IF-MATCH, counter row TASK-<year> created by the first claim of the year), addressed through Flow Configuration (DATASET_SEQUENCE_COUNTERS_*). If no number can be claimed the task is not created and the run takes the existing Task Processing catch, which records the error.
- §10.2 TASK_QUEUE: the task row carries its Entity Key, TaskRef, ParentKey and RootKey REC:<the document's record key> (DGO DIGITAL OPS rows carry the master record's key; empty for a row the Phase 5 backfill has not reached), RootRef (the record's ReferenceId), IdState ACTIVE, Rev 1, the Request ID as CorrelationId and CreatedByRequest, and ClientRequestHash when the request carries one (B3). The task type and grouping, which a second Update item wrote straight after the create, are written by the create itself, so that update is removed (it is a governed row: B9).
- S3: new tasks have no composite reference. Compose_ReferenceID, which the e-mails, the acknowledgement link's ref= text and the task/document pairs show, is now the Task Reference. The composite <yyyyMMdd>-<doc ID>-<category>-<sub-category>-<task ID> was never stored, so nothing that resolves a task changes; the acknowledgement link finds the task by its item= value, as before.
- Review C-1 (2026-10-02): assigning a document no longer erases its AI extraction. Update_item_Doc wrote BodyExtract and TextExtraxt as empty text; both keys are removed, and Update item leaves fields it is not given unchanged.
- Review C-2 (2026-10-02): Compose_Config_BaseURL held a Markdown link, [https://taskack.page.gd](https://taskack.page.gd), so the acknowledgement link built from it was broken. It is now the address itself.
- Tenant defect 2026-10-10 (TASK-2026-00002, run 08584100110433772866731334335CU24): the e-mail greeted "Dear ,". Compose_AssignedToTitle_Value took coalesce() of its candidates, and coalesce() skips only nulls: the department match came back as empty text and won. It now takes the first candidate that is not empty, ending with "Officer".
- Tenant defect 2026-10-10: Handling Status and Response Priority both read "Standard Official Review" on every normal task, because both fell back to that text. Response Priority now states the response window it describes: "Priority Review Window" for critical, urgent or high, otherwise "Standard Response Window". Handling Status is unchanged.
- Tenant defect 2026-10-10: the Support Access link sent ref=TASK-<item ID> (TASK-16167) while the e-mail itself shows the Task Reference (TASK-2026-00002). The link now carries the Task Reference, Compose_ReferenceID, and keeps item=<ID> for the lookup.
- Deep links: task e-mail links start at https://folio-platform.page.gd (the Workspace's primary host, owner 2026-10-08), not https://taskack.page.gd.
- Set variable values held in a Compose step (the designer dropped inline and changed Set variable values on paste; tenant export of IP_Create__Task__for_received_Email_Endpoint, 6 October 2026): Set_variable_varData_Validation_Failure, Set_variable_varRequestId, Set_variable_varStatusCode.
- B5 (e-mail template package, ITEM-92): removed 3 unread steps that load images from third-party hosts (Compose_Email_Notification_Template, Compose_Email_Notification_Template_2, Compose_Email_Notification_2); nothing reads them, and the steps that ran after them run after their predecessors.
- ITEM-66: every mail send writes a receipt to Portal Outbox Receipts (Send_an_email_(V2)_Main_5): message type, recipient (the send's own To), the run as reference, sent or failed, and the error on failure; never the message body. Compose_<send>_Outcome fails exactly when the send failed, so the scope around it ends as it did before the receipt was added and the flow's catch path still fires.
- ITEM-77 (owner decision, 2026-10-06): every Office 365 step signs in as the registry mailbox, dgsregistry@nitda.gov.ng, connection c0b9e7a5 (Send_an_email_(V2)_Main_5 used another connection).

### BULK_ASSIGNMENT

- Each document goes through the task steps of the Single_Task_Assignment package above: the task row in Global Tracking Queue with its identity columns, the document row in DGO DIGITAL OPS (Processed, its AI extraction kept: C-1), the assignee's title from Departments, and one notification to the assignee with the task's acknowledgement link. A bulk task and a single task are the same record.
- T7 / §8.2: the Task References for the whole batch are claimed once, by the generation kit, before any task is created: N consecutive TASK-YYYY-NNNNN numbers from the TASK-<year> counter. Each document is paired with its number before the loop, so a document keeps its number whatever happens to the others. If no numbers can be claimed the reply is 503 RETRY_LATER and nothing is created.
- Folio's payload is read as it sends it (core/assignment-payload.js, dgo-bulk-assignment-payload/v2: ids, category, categoryCode, subcategory, subcategoryCode, assignedTo, assignedToDsu, supportingAssignee, supportingDsu, ccRecipients, priority, startDate, ack, due, instruction, requestedBy). Compose_Bulk_Task holds those values under the names the task steps read; per document, the activity and document IDs are the document's own and the title and attachment link come from its DGO DIGITAL OPS row.
- G-04: the caller is resolved as every identification package resolves it (see "Caller identity" above), from the sign-in proof or, while IDENTITY_PROOF_REQUIRED is not true, from userEmail or requestedBy. With the switch true, a caller who is not an active directory user is refused with 401 and one whose role does not allow bulk-assignment (or bulk:assign) with 403, before any number is claimed. The batch's requester (AssignedBy, the failure e-mail) is that caller.
- The request is refused with 400 unless it names 1 to 50 documents (Folio's own limit, config/app.config.js maxBulkAssign), an assignee e-mail address and a category.
- The reply (202 with the claimed references, or 400, 503, 500) is sent before any task is created, with Access-Control-Allow-Origin from Flow Configuration's ALLOWED_ORIGIN rows, as the flow's data-retrieval reply did. The documents are then assigned one after another. A document whose task or update fails is recorded with its reference in varErrors and the rest go on; if any failed, the requester (requestedBy, else dgs@nitda.gov.ng) gets one e-mail listing them.
- S8 / ID-19: the run sets its own Request ID (varRequestId = guid()) first; the reply, the task rows and the failure e-mail carry it. Nothing the client sends is adopted.
- Set variable values held in a Compose step (the designer dropped inline and changed Set variable values on paste; tenant export of IP_Create__Task__for_received_Email_Endpoint, 6 October 2026): Set_variable_varData_Bulk_Accepted, Set_variable_varData_Bulk_Empty, Set_variable_varData_Bulk_Invalid, Set_variable_varData_Bulk_Retry.
- Administrative e-mail goes to the registry mailbox (owner decision, 2026-10-06): the fixed recipients Send_Bulk_Failure_Email.To are set to dgsregistry@nitda.gov.ng (the bulk-failure fallback was dgs@nitda.gov.ng). The configurable ones stay read from Flow Configuration (NOTIFY_OPS_TO, NOTIFY_REGISTRY_TO, NOTIFY_HELPDESK_TO), which fall back to the registry mailbox when blank.
- ITEM-66: every mail send writes a receipt to Portal Outbox Receipts (Send_Bulk_Failure_Email): message type, recipient (the send's own To), the run as reference, sent or failed, and the error on failure; never the message body. Compose_<send>_Outcome fails exactly when the send failed, so the scope around it ends as it did before the receipt was added and the flow's catch path still fires.
- ITEM-77 (owner decision, 2026-10-06): every Office 365 step signs in as the registry mailbox, dgsregistry@nitda.gov.ng, connection c0b9e7a5 (Send_an_email_(V2)_Main_5, Send_Bulk_Failure_Email used another connection).

The scope is new: it replaces the flow's Scope_Global as a whole (175 steps).

**Test after pasting.** Assign three documents to one officer from Folio's Bulk Assignment. The reply is 202 with three consecutive TASK-YYYY-NNNNN references; in Global Tracking Queue three new rows carry those TaskRefs, each with its own EntityKey, IdState ACTIVE and Rev 1; each document row shows AssignmentStatus Processed and keeps its BodyExtract; the officer receives three e-mails, one per task; Portal Sequence Counters' TASK-<year> row advanced by three in one claim. Then send one document ID that does not exist with two that do: two tasks are created and the requester receives one e-mail naming the missing one.

### FETCH_ALL

- S8 / ID-19: the run sets its own Request ID (varRequestId = guid()) first. The flow declared it as the client's requestId when one was sent.
- G-04: the caller is resolved as every identification package resolves it (see "Caller identity" above): from the sign-in proof when one is valid; else, while IDENTITY_PROOF_REQUIRED is not true, from userEmail as today. With the switch true and no valid proof, the flow's own unknown-caller branch answers 401. The role is read from the directory row's Role choice, which the flow read as text and so never matched a RoleId.
- §10.2: every record the Workspace reads carries its identity. Documents: EntityKey, ReferenceId, IdState. Tasks: EntityKey, TaskRef, ParentKey, RootKey, RootRef, IdState, Rev. Comments (minutes): EntityKey, ParentKey, RootKey, RootRef, AuthorKey. The fields already returned are unchanged.
- §13 Phase 4: FETCH_ALL also returns register, briefs, meetings, projects, approvals, files: the latest 500 rows of Portal Registry, DGO_Briefs, DGO_Meetings, DGO_Projects, DGO_Approvals and DGO_RegistryFiles, each with its Entity Key and reference, addressed through Flow Configuration (DATASET_<KEY>_*). A collection whose list cannot be read comes back empty and the rest of the reply is unaffected. approvals, which was always empty, now holds DGO_Approvals rows in the shape Folio's approvals view reads.
- Directory and reference data as Folio reads them, ported from the retired DGO_FETCH_ALL design (registers/flow-retirement.json): the directory is read in pages to 5,000 rows (it holds 852; one GetItems page is 500), Role, Persona and Status are served as text rather than Choice objects, and Departments and Categories, imported from spreadsheets so GetItems returns field_1…field_N, are read by those internal names. The keys Folio reads are unchanged.
- ITEM-90 (owner approval 2026-10-08): every active directory user is admitted and receives the slice of data their role allows; until now only roles carrying "*" or user:view were admitted (systemAdmin and userAdmin: the operator and 822 active viewers got 403), and whoever was admitted received everything. Tiers, from the directory row: all (systemAdmin, userAdmin, executive, operator, which is the registry role, or the admin, executive or registry persona) receives what it did; every other caller receives the tasks assigned to them, read from Global Tracking Queue by the indexed AssignedTo so older assignments are included, the documents those tasks name (read by ID, up to 60), and those documents' comments. A director also receives approvals; their directorate's tasks are not read, because Global Tracking Queue holds its 20 indexed columns and GDSUROUT is not one of them (follow-up). The directory goes to every caller, with e-mail addresses only for the all tier and on the caller's own row. Portal submissions, briefs, meetings, projects and registry files go to the all tier only. Tasks now carry RoutedDsu (GDSUROUT).
- Owner decision 2026-10-18: the Workspace's System Health shows failed notices. FETCH_ALL returns failureHealth, the JSON Folio_Failure_Watch writes to Flow Configuration NOTIFY_FAILURE_HEALTH (the open count per group, the broken-connection flag and the time of the check), to the all tier only; null when the row is absent or unreadable. One row of a few hundred characters: the reply grows by that and nothing else.
- Tenant defect (8 October 2026): the newest 500 tasks are read by ID, not Modified. Global Tracking Queue holds 16,071 rows and already carries the 20 indexed columns SharePoint allows, none of them Modified, so "Modified desc" exceeded the list view threshold: Get_All_Tasks failed, every read after it was skipped, and the flow answered 200 with null collections, so the Workspace loaded empty. ID is always indexed.
- ITEM-74 (owner decision 2026-10-10): FETCH_ALL carries the registry inbox. For the all tier (the registry, admin and executive roles) it reads the newest 50 messages of the registry mailbox's Inbox (Office 365 Get emails (V3), as Fetch_Emails_POST does, no attachments) and returns id, subject, sender, received time, preview, importance, conversation, internetMessageId and whether it has attachments, so Lookup can raise a task from an e-mail (EMAIL_RELATED_TASK). Other tiers receive none. A failed read leaves the list empty; the rest of the reply is unchanged.
- ITEM-52: the Response_FetchAll run record carries the reply's size instead of the reply, and the read endpoint no longer e-mails its run record (owner decision 2026-10-06; tenant evidence 2026-10-10).
- Set variable values held in a Compose step (the designer dropped inline and changed Set variable values on paste; tenant export of IP_Create__Task__for_received_Email_Endpoint, 6 October 2026): Set_variable_varData_FetchAll_Catch, Set_variable_varData_FetchAll_Denied_401, Set_variable_varData_FetchAll_Denied_403, Set_variable_varData_FetchAll_Success, Set_variable_varRequestId.
- The sign-in proof is redacted from the run record (tenant defect, 8 October 2026): Compose_Redacted_Headers masked Authorization but not X-DGO-Proof, where the proof travels since release 9, so every telemetry row held a usable session token.

### DYNAMIC_ACTIONS

- S8 / ID-19: the Request ID is the flow's own guid(). It was the client's X-Correlation-ID or requestId whenever one was sent; that value is now kept only as clientCorrelationId (sanitised, 64 characters).
- G-04: the caller is resolved as every identification package resolves it (see "Caller identity" above): from the sign-in proof when one is valid; else, while IDENTITY_PROOF_REQUIRED is not true, from userEmail as today. With the switch true and no valid proof, the gate answers 401. The role is read from the directory row's Role choice, which the flow read as text and so never matched a RoleId.
- The request may now carry, at its top level or under payload, the fields the identity operations read: entityType, entityKey, target, survivor, fromKey, toKey, linkType, title, text, localKey, parentKey, reason, toOrgKey, movementAction, subject, senderEmail, channel, locatorKind, locatorContainer, locatorValue, legacyNumber, decision and clientRequestHash.
- The gate serves the new operations (register, upsert-record, open-file, move-file, link, void, reparent, merge; underscores are read as hyphens, so upsert_record is upsert-record). upsert-record leaves the recognised-but-unserved set. Routes the caller's role must allow: register and link need correspondence; upsert-record needs briefs, meetings, projects, approvals or orchestrator (minutes) by entity type; open-file, move-file, void and reparent need registry; merge needs registry-merge (Registry Manager only, §9: add "registry-merge" to that role's AllowedRoutesJson; "*" also passes).
- Each new operation is checked before anything is written; a request that fails is refused with 400 and the reason. register: a subject. upsert-record: entity type MIN, BRF, MTG, PRJ, APR or RMD (a reminder: assignedTo and dueAt, written once); a title (or, for a minute, its text and its task as parentKey TSK:<key>) unless entityKey names the row to change. open-file: a title. move-file: the file as target and toOrgKey. link: fromKey and toKey as Qualified Keys and one of the 11 link types. void: a target and a reason. reparent: a target ATT, TSK, MIN or APR Qualified Key and the new parentKey. merge: the absorbed record as target and the survivor, two different REC Qualified Keys. A target is a Qualified Key TYPE:<guid> or spo:<listGuid>/<itemId> (B10); a bare item ID, RefIDD or title is refused.
- T11 / B3: a replayed request (the same idempotency key; Folio sends its clientRequestHash as that key) returns the first result unchanged. Every new operation stores its result on its audit event, and the replay answer is that result; older events, which hold none, keep the replay answer they had.
- ITEM-81 (from the hardened scope): an idempotency key already used for a different operation answers 409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT and nothing is replayed or written; only the same request gets the first result back.
- register (§8.2, S7): registers a record received outside the portal (Folio, e-mail, library). A request whose clientRequestHash Portal Registry already holds returns that record. Otherwise it claims the next NITDA-YYYY-NNNNN (the kit claim, floored at the register's highest number) and writes the Portal Registry row: Title and ReferenceId, Subject, Channel (one of the catalogue's channel codes, else internal), CorrespondenceType Incoming, SenderEmail, Status received, EntityKey, IdState ACTIVE, Rev 1, Direction In, CorrelationId, CreatedByRequest, ClientRequestHash and, when sent, SourceLocator. A locator (locatorKind EXO_INTERNET_MESSAGE_ID, SPO_ITEM, ODB_ITEM or PAPER_FILE, with locatorContainer and locatorValue; for an e-mail, the registry mailbox and the internetMessageId, T8) is written to DGO_IdentityMap as a LOCATOR entry: System from the catalogue, MatchKey LOCATOR|<kind>|<container>|<value> (§10.2), not written again when that key exists. If the row cannot be written a VOID row accounts for the number (Q2) and the reply is 500; if no number can be claimed, 503. The audit event REGISTERED carries REC:<key>.
- upsert_record (§7, §13): creates or changes a minute, brief, meeting, project or approval. With entityKey it changes that row's Title (a minute's Description, an approval's Decision) by the kit's Guarded Update (Rev + 1); without, it creates the row with a new Entity Key, IdState ACTIVE, Rev 1, CreatedByRequest and ClientRequestHash (CorrelationId where the list has it), after returning the existing row if its clientRequestHash is already there. A minute (Task_Comments) is created under its task: ParentKey TSK:<key>, RootKey and RootRef from the task row, RefIDD the task's document, Description the text, AuthorKey USR:<the caller>; an unknown task is 404. An approval takes Decision (Pending unless sent) and, when parentKey is given, ParentKey and RootKey. When Folio sends its own local key (localKey), DGO_IdentityMap gets a FOLIO_LOCAL_KEY alias, System runtime, MatchKey ALIAS|FOLIO_LOCAL_KEY||<key> (§12.3 4a).
- open_file (§8.2, T12): opens a registry file. A request whose clientRequestHash DGO_RegistryFiles already holds returns that file. Otherwise it claims the next FILE-YYYY-NNNNN (the kit claim, counter FILE-<year>) and writes the file: Title, RegistryFileRef, CurrentHolder (toOrgKey, else the caller), EntityKey, IdState ACTIVE, Rev 1, CorrelationId, CreatedByRequest, ClientRequestHash; then the OPENED movement in DGO_FileMovements; and, when Folio sends the file's old DGO/YYYY/NNNNNN number (legacyNumber), a LEGACY_REGISTRY_FILE_NO alias (MatchKey ALIAS|LEGACY_REGISTRY_FILE_NO||<number>). If the file cannot be written a VOID row accounts for the number and the reply is 500; if no number can be claimed, 503.
- move_file (T12): moves a registry file to toOrgKey. The file (REG:<key> or its spo: locator) is found in DGO_RegistryFiles; its CurrentHolder changes by the Guarded Update (Rev + 1) and DGO_FileMovements gets a MOVED event: SubjectKey and RootKey REG:<key>, RootRef the FILE reference, FromOrgKey (the holder before), ToOrgKey, MovementAction (as sent, else MOVED), RevAfter. An unknown file is 404; a file changed three times during the move is 409.
- link (§6, T12): writes a DGO_RecordLinks row: FromKey, LinkType, ToKey, LinkMatchKey <from>|<type>|<to> (unique), EntityKey, IdState ACTIVE, Rev 1, CreatedByRequest. A link that already exists is returned (existing: true), not written twice.
- void (§9): sets the target's IdState to VOID by the Guarded Update (Rev + 1) and writes VoidReason where the list has it (Portal Registry). The row is kept and its reference is never reissued. The audit event VOIDED carries the reason. A target already void is answered unchanged.
- reparent (§9): moves an attachment, task, minute or approval under a new parent. ParentKey becomes parentKey; RootKey becomes parentKey when the new parent is a REC or CAS, else stays as it was. Guarded Update (Rev + 1); audit event REPARENTED with the old and new parent.
- merge (§9 merge procedure, T9; Registry Manager only): absorbs record A (target) into survivor B. 1. LNK A MERGED_INTO B. 2. A's attachments (Portal Attachments, ParentKey REC:A) and tasks (Global Tracking Queue, ParentKey or RootKey REC:A) are re-parented to B, each by the Guarded Update with RootRef B's reference and an audit event REPARENTED. 3. A: IdState MERGED and, where the list has it, SupersededBy REC:B, by the Guarded Update (Rev + 1). 4. Audit event MERGED on A and on B. A's reference resolves to B from then on. Either record unknown is 404; a record already merged or void cannot be merged (409).
- The reply (Compose_Outcome) takes the result of whichever new operation ran, as it does for the live ones.
- ITEM-25 (owner decision 2026-10-08, on the needs assessment): dispatch, dispatchoutbound and archivereference are served by transitionstatus instead of answering 501. A letter goes out through the DGO Correspondence Mailer; dispatch records the document as Treated (the Status column offers Treated and Not Treated). archivereference records it as Treated and sets its IdState to ARCHIVED (the catalogue's lifecycle state), before the unchanged check so an already treated document is still archived. The caller's role must allow the dispatch route (dispatch) or the archive route (archive). The audit row names the operation asked for.
- Gap found 2026-10-10: a task's assignee whose role lacks the My Work route (Read-only Viewer, Executive: 852 of 854 people) could acknowledge a task but never start, update or complete it, because update-task required the orchestrator route at the gate. The gate now lets update-task through for any active role, and the update-task case decides once the task is read: a role with the orchestrator route (or "*") may update any task, as before; anyone else only a task assigned to them, and is refused 403 otherwise.
- ITEM-25: the activity lifecycle steps (activity-archive, activity-siwes, activity-nysc :create-queue-record, :set-reference-id, :update-activity) are served by IP_Activity_Lifecycle_Endpoint (ACTIVITY_LIFECYCLE); here they are refused as unknown (400), not as recognised-but-unserved (501).
- The sign-in proof is redacted from the run record (tenant defect, 8 October 2026): Compose_Redacted_Headers masked Authorization but not X-DGO-Proof, where the proof travels since release 9, so every telemetry row held a usable session token.
- ITEM-66: every mail send writes a receipt to Portal Outbox Receipts (Send_Server_Error_Alert_Email): message type, recipient (the send's own To), the run as reference, sent or failed, and the error on failure; never the message body. Compose_<send>_Outcome fails exactly when the send failed, so the scope around it ends as it did before the receipt was added and the flow's catch path still fires.

**Test after pasting.** From Folio (or any client signed in as an active directory user), send: register {subject, channel email, locatorKind EXO_INTERNET_MESSAGE_ID, locatorContainer <the registry mailbox>, locatorValue <an internetMessageId>} → a NITDA-YYYY-NNNNN and a REC key, a Portal Registry row and a DGO_IdentityMap LOCATOR row; upsert_record {entityType MIN, parentKey TSK:<a task's EntityKey>, text} → a Task_Comments row under that task; open_file {title} → FILE-YYYY-NNNNN; link {fromKey REC:…, toKey REG:…, linkType FILED_IN}; move_file twice {target REG:…, toOrgKey} → two MOVED rows in DGO_FileMovements (T12). Send any of them again with the same clientRequestHash: the first result comes back with replayed true and nothing new is written (T11). merge two test records as a Registry Manager (T9).

### USER_ADMIN

- S8 / ID-19: the Request ID is the flow's own guid(). It was the client's X-Correlation-ID or requestId whenever one was sent; that value is now kept only as clientCorrelationId (sanitised, 64 characters).
- G-04: the caller is resolved as every identification package resolves it (see "Caller identity" above): from the sign-in proof when one is valid; else, while IDENTITY_PROOF_REQUIRED is not true, from userEmail as today. With the switch true and no valid proof, the gate answers 401. The role is read from the directory row's Role choice, which the flow read as text and so never matched a RoleId.
- The request may now carry, at its top level or under payload, the fields the identity operations read: entityType, entityKey, target, survivor, fromKey, toKey, linkType, title, text, localKey, parentKey, reason, toOrgKey, movementAction, subject, senderEmail, channel, locatorKind, locatorContainer, locatorValue, legacyNumber, decision and clientRequestHash.
- The gate serves the new operations (register, upsert-record, open-file, move-file, link, void, reparent, merge; underscores are read as hyphens, so upsert_record is upsert-record). upsert-record leaves the recognised-but-unserved set. Routes the caller's role must allow: register and link need correspondence; upsert-record needs briefs, meetings, projects, approvals or orchestrator (minutes) by entity type; open-file, move-file, void and reparent need registry; merge needs registry-merge (Registry Manager only, §9: add "registry-merge" to that role's AllowedRoutesJson; "*" also passes).
- Each new operation is checked before anything is written; a request that fails is refused with 400 and the reason. register: a subject. upsert-record: entity type MIN, BRF, MTG, PRJ, APR or RMD (a reminder: assignedTo and dueAt, written once); a title (or, for a minute, its text and its task as parentKey TSK:<key>) unless entityKey names the row to change. open-file: a title. move-file: the file as target and toOrgKey. link: fromKey and toKey as Qualified Keys and one of the 11 link types. void: a target and a reason. reparent: a target ATT, TSK, MIN or APR Qualified Key and the new parentKey. merge: the absorbed record as target and the survivor, two different REC Qualified Keys. A target is a Qualified Key TYPE:<guid> or spo:<listGuid>/<itemId> (B10); a bare item ID, RefIDD or title is refused.
- T11 / B3: a replayed request (the same idempotency key; Folio sends its clientRequestHash as that key) returns the first result unchanged. Every new operation stores its result on its audit event, and the replay answer is that result; older events, which hold none, keep the replay answer they had.
- ITEM-81 (from the hardened scope): an idempotency key already used for a different operation answers 409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT and nothing is replayed or written; only the same request gets the first result back.
- register (§8.2, S7): registers a record received outside the portal (Folio, e-mail, library). A request whose clientRequestHash Portal Registry already holds returns that record. Otherwise it claims the next NITDA-YYYY-NNNNN (the kit claim, floored at the register's highest number) and writes the Portal Registry row: Title and ReferenceId, Subject, Channel (one of the catalogue's channel codes, else internal), CorrespondenceType Incoming, SenderEmail, Status received, EntityKey, IdState ACTIVE, Rev 1, Direction In, CorrelationId, CreatedByRequest, ClientRequestHash and, when sent, SourceLocator. A locator (locatorKind EXO_INTERNET_MESSAGE_ID, SPO_ITEM, ODB_ITEM or PAPER_FILE, with locatorContainer and locatorValue; for an e-mail, the registry mailbox and the internetMessageId, T8) is written to DGO_IdentityMap as a LOCATOR entry: System from the catalogue, MatchKey LOCATOR|<kind>|<container>|<value> (§10.2), not written again when that key exists. If the row cannot be written a VOID row accounts for the number (Q2) and the reply is 500; if no number can be claimed, 503. The audit event REGISTERED carries REC:<key>.
- upsert_record (§7, §13): creates or changes a minute, brief, meeting, project or approval. With entityKey it changes that row's Title (a minute's Description, an approval's Decision) by the kit's Guarded Update (Rev + 1); without, it creates the row with a new Entity Key, IdState ACTIVE, Rev 1, CreatedByRequest and ClientRequestHash (CorrelationId where the list has it), after returning the existing row if its clientRequestHash is already there. A minute (Task_Comments) is created under its task: ParentKey TSK:<key>, RootKey and RootRef from the task row, RefIDD the task's document, Description the text, AuthorKey USR:<the caller>; an unknown task is 404. An approval takes Decision (Pending unless sent) and, when parentKey is given, ParentKey and RootKey. When Folio sends its own local key (localKey), DGO_IdentityMap gets a FOLIO_LOCAL_KEY alias, System runtime, MatchKey ALIAS|FOLIO_LOCAL_KEY||<key> (§12.3 4a).
- open_file (§8.2, T12): opens a registry file. A request whose clientRequestHash DGO_RegistryFiles already holds returns that file. Otherwise it claims the next FILE-YYYY-NNNNN (the kit claim, counter FILE-<year>) and writes the file: Title, RegistryFileRef, CurrentHolder (toOrgKey, else the caller), EntityKey, IdState ACTIVE, Rev 1, CorrelationId, CreatedByRequest, ClientRequestHash; then the OPENED movement in DGO_FileMovements; and, when Folio sends the file's old DGO/YYYY/NNNNNN number (legacyNumber), a LEGACY_REGISTRY_FILE_NO alias (MatchKey ALIAS|LEGACY_REGISTRY_FILE_NO||<number>). If the file cannot be written a VOID row accounts for the number and the reply is 500; if no number can be claimed, 503.
- move_file (T12): moves a registry file to toOrgKey. The file (REG:<key> or its spo: locator) is found in DGO_RegistryFiles; its CurrentHolder changes by the Guarded Update (Rev + 1) and DGO_FileMovements gets a MOVED event: SubjectKey and RootKey REG:<key>, RootRef the FILE reference, FromOrgKey (the holder before), ToOrgKey, MovementAction (as sent, else MOVED), RevAfter. An unknown file is 404; a file changed three times during the move is 409.
- link (§6, T12): writes a DGO_RecordLinks row: FromKey, LinkType, ToKey, LinkMatchKey <from>|<type>|<to> (unique), EntityKey, IdState ACTIVE, Rev 1, CreatedByRequest. A link that already exists is returned (existing: true), not written twice.
- void (§9): sets the target's IdState to VOID by the Guarded Update (Rev + 1) and writes VoidReason where the list has it (Portal Registry). The row is kept and its reference is never reissued. The audit event VOIDED carries the reason. A target already void is answered unchanged.
- reparent (§9): moves an attachment, task, minute or approval under a new parent. ParentKey becomes parentKey; RootKey becomes parentKey when the new parent is a REC or CAS, else stays as it was. Guarded Update (Rev + 1); audit event REPARENTED with the old and new parent.
- merge (§9 merge procedure, T9; Registry Manager only): absorbs record A (target) into survivor B. 1. LNK A MERGED_INTO B. 2. A's attachments (Portal Attachments, ParentKey REC:A) and tasks (Global Tracking Queue, ParentKey or RootKey REC:A) are re-parented to B, each by the Guarded Update with RootRef B's reference and an audit event REPARENTED. 3. A: IdState MERGED and, where the list has it, SupersededBy REC:B, by the Guarded Update (Rev + 1). 4. Audit event MERGED on A and on B. A's reference resolves to B from then on. Either record unknown is 404; a record already merged or void cannot be merged (409).
- ITEM-25 user-admin (needs assessment 2026-10-08: the User Administration screen's changes queued on the device and never reached DGO_UserDirectory, so a person could be added or given a role only in SharePoint itself): user-admin:create-user, update-user, assign-role and disable-user are served. The caller's role must allow the user-admin route. The person is found by e-mail. create-user writes a new directory row (UserId, EntityKey, IdState ACTIVE, Rev 1, CreatedAt/By) and is refused 409 when the address is already there; the others change the row by Guarded Update (Rev + 1) and are refused 404 when it is not. Role, Persona and Status must be the directory's own choices (400). Only a systemAdmin grants systemAdmin or changes a systemAdmin's row (403). Each change is audited as user:<action> with the officer as actor.
- The reply (Compose_Outcome) takes the result of whichever new operation ran, as it does for the live ones.
- The sign-in proof is redacted from the run record (tenant defect, 8 October 2026): Compose_Redacted_Headers masked Authorization but not X-DGO-Proof, where the proof travels since release 9, so every telemetry row held a usable session token.
- ITEM-66: every mail send writes a receipt to Portal Outbox Receipts (Send_Server_Error_Alert_Email): message type, recipient (the send's own To), the run as reference, sent or failed, and the error on failure; never the message body. Compose_<send>_Outcome fails exactly when the send failed, so the scope around it ends as it did before the receipt was added and the flow's catch path still fires.

- ITEM-25 (owner decision 2026-10-10): activity-archive, activity-siwes and activity-nysc are served, as the Canvas Activities screen did them, in the three steps Folio sends. The activity is read from DGO DIGITAL OPS by its item ID (404 if absent). create-queue-record writes a Global Tracking Queue row built from that activity, not from the request: Title, ActivityTrackingID (its RefIDD), RefIDD and RefIDDN (its ID), AttachmentLink, StartDate, DueDate and Acknowledgement Due Date today, AssignedBy DGS OFFICE, AssignedTo dgs@NITDA.gov.ng, Status Completed, Priority Low, NVERSE DGOFASTTRACK, Category (Archived, Internships (SIWES) or Internships (NYSC)), EntityKey and IdState ACTIVE, and answers its ID. set-reference-id reads that queue row back and refuses (409) one that is not this activity's DGOFASTTRACK row of that category, then sets Reference_ID to yyyyMMdd(tomorrow, WAT)-<activity ID>-<UNC | INT-SIWES | INT-NYSC>-<queue ID>, computed here. update-activity marks the activity Treated, AssignmentStatus Processed (the list offers Processed and Pending; Canvas wrote Assigned), AssignedTo dgs@NITDA.gov.ng and the category. Each step writes an audit event carrying its result, so a repeated request returns the first result (T11). The caller's role must allow the activities route.

### EMAIL_RELATED_TASK

- Folio's request reaches the flow: core/data-client.js sends {action, payload:{…}, userEmail, requestId}, with the e-mail as payload.email and the task fields flat in payload (core/assignment-payload.js buildEmailTaskPayload), while every step of the flow read Email.id and NewActivityTask.* at the top level. Folio's requests therefore carried no e-mail id and were refused at validation. Compose_Email_Task_Input, the scope's first step, gives the steps the fields they read, from the top-level form when a request carries it and from Folio's payload otherwise (priority capitalised and status New, as the Assignment Desk sends them), and every step reads it instead of the trigger.
- S8 / ID-19: every run mints its Request ID. varRequestId took the client's requestId whenever the request carried one (Folio always sends one), so the reply, the audit and every row written carried a value the client chose. The scope now sets it to guid() before anything reads it.
- G-04: the caller is resolved as every identification package resolves it (see "Caller identity" above): from the sign-in proof when one is valid; else, while IDENTITY_PROOF_REQUIRED is not true, from the request (userEmail, else Folio's createdBy). With the switch true, a caller who is not an active directory user is refused with 401 and one whose role does not allow single-assignment (the Folio route that owns create-task-from-email, config/action-ownership.config.js) with 403, through the flow's own validation-failure path, before any number is claimed or any row written. The task's AssignedBy is that caller.
- B1: the audit e-mail's attachment list is built without a Filter array, which a pasted scope may not hold. Select_Audit_Attachments turns each attachment with a name and content into its JSON text and Compose_Audit_Attachments joins them into the same list Filter_array_Compose_Data_FlowRun_Verification_Email_Attachments gave.
- S3 / §8.2: each task gets a Task Reference TASK-YYYY-NNNNN, claimed by the generation kit (10 flat attempts, IF-MATCH, counter row TASK-<year> created by the first claim of the year), addressed through Flow Configuration (DATASET_SEQUENCE_COUNTERS_*). If no number can be claimed the task is not created and the run takes the existing Task Processing catch, which records the error.
- §7.1 / §15: the task names its e-mail's record when the e-mail is registered. The e-mail's internetMessageId (Get_Email) is looked up in DGO_IdentityMap as an EXO_INTERNET_MESSAGE_ID LOCATOR, which DYNAMIC_ACTIONS register writes (T8); when it points at a REC, the task's ParentKey and RootKey are that REC and RootRef its NITDA-YYYY-NNNNN from Portal Registry. An e-mail no one has registered gives an empty ParentKey, and the task still keeps the message id in ActivityTrackingID and RefIDD, as before. No map entry is written here: an e-mail's locator belongs to its record (§7.1), and one written for a task would block the e-mail's registration. A failed lookup does not stop the task.
- §10.2 TASK_QUEUE: the task is created in Global Tracking Queue (ee82725a-c408-45e2-a8e8-facf7a092047), the list Folio reads tasks from (FETCH_ALL) and Single and Bulk Assignment write. The flow created it in DEV_OPS_Global_Tracking_Queue (22c4e38d-5040-4e0f-aa47-dd3aa3f28abf), a test list (owner direction, 5 October 2026; spec 1.2.4), so a task raised from an e-mail never appeared in Folio, and then Update_item_Task_Email wrote the reference and task type into Global Tracking Queue at the test list's item ID — onto whichever unrelated task holds that ID there. The create now carries the task type and grouping itself, the Entity Key, TaskRef, ParentKey, RootKey, RootRef, IdState ACTIVE, Rev 1, the Request ID as CorrelationId and CreatedByRequest, ClientRequestHash (B3), and Reference_ID, the legacy reference column, holding the Task Reference until Phase 6; the update is removed (B9).
- The task's DueDate is written. It was null unless the due date was given as a non-text value, which JSON never does, and its expression called type(), which is not a workflow expression function, so the step could not evaluate it. DueDate is now the given due date (TaskDueDate, else TaskDue) in yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ssZ, or empty when none is given.
- StartDate and the acknowledgement due date no longer fail when the request gives none. Each chose between a default and formatDateTime(<the given date>), and an expression evaluates both branches of if(), so an absent date stopped the create. The given date is now read as 1900-01-01 where it is empty, in the branch that is then not taken; the defaults are unchanged.
- S3: new tasks have no composite reference. Compose_ReferenceID (<yyyyMMdd>-EML-<category>-<sub-category>-<item ID>), which the e-mails and the reply show, is now the Task Reference, and the acknowledgement and support links' ref= is the Task Reference instead of TASK-<item ID> (support.html?ref=TASK-YYYY-NNNNN, §5 ID-05); the links still find the task by item=. The reply's data carries taskRef and entityKey.
- ITEM-50 (owner decision, 2026-10-06): the two task notifications go to the assigned officer, the task row's AssignedTo (the request's assignee when the row has none), with the third-assignee Cc kept. They went to one named address whoever the task was for.
- ITEM-50 / ITEM-52 (owner decision, 2026-10-06): the diagnostics mail (Send_an_email_(V2)_Main_1_1, the raw response to one named address) and the two audit mails (Send_an_email_(V2)_Audit and _Audit_1, which repeated what the audit lists hold) are removed, with Scope_Build_Audit_information, which built nothing else. The reply to the caller is unchanged.
- Deep links: task e-mail links start at https://folio-platform.page.gd (the Workspace's primary host, owner 2026-10-08), not https://taskack.page.gd.
- Tenant defect 2026-10-12: a task raised from an e-mail sent the assignee two near-identical notices (Send_an_email_(V2)_Main_1_1_1, then Scope_3's Send_an_email_(V2)_Main_1_1_2, the same task and links). Scope_3 is removed, so one task sends one notice; the notification count follows the one send.
- Set variable values held in a Compose step (the designer dropped inline and changed Set variable values on paste; tenant export of IP_Create__Task__for_received_Email_Endpoint, 6 October 2026): Set_variable_varData_Success, Set_variable_varData_Task_Processing_Catch, Set_variable_varEmailId, Set_variable_varRequestId, Set_variable_varStatusCode.
- ITEM-66: every mail send writes a receipt to Portal Outbox Receipts (Send_an_email_(V2)_Main_1_1_1): message type, recipient (the send's own To), the run as reference, sent or failed, and the error on failure; never the message body. Compose_<send>_Outcome fails exactly when the send failed, so the scope around it ends as it did before the receipt was added and the flow's catch path still fires.
- ITEM-77 (owner decision, 2026-10-06): every Office 365 step signs in as the registry mailbox, dgsregistry@nitda.gov.ng, connection c0b9e7a5 (Send_an_email_(V2)_Main_1_1_1, Get_Email used another connection).

### OTP_VERIFY

- Tenant defect (8 October 2026): a verify for an address with no code issued answered 500, because Update_item_Attempts had no row to count against (id empty). The attempt count is now written only when an unverified code exists; otherwise the flow goes straight to its no-pending-code answer, as a wrong code does, and nothing is written.
- The response data is an object. The flow built it in varResponse, a string, and returned that string as data, so Folio (core/contracts.js liftEnvelope) could not read any field of it, the proof included. Set_variable_varData now parses it; every value the flow appends to varResponse is one JSON object.
- G-04, the mint: when the code verifies, the caller is looked up in DGO_UserDirectory (active rows only). An active directory user gets a proof: a guid() token written to the proof ledger (Purpose internal-session, unconsumed) with an expiry of 4 hours (AUTHENTICATION_CONTRACT.md §2a), and the reply carries token, expiresAt (the same Compose, so the ledger row and the reply agree) and claims read from the directory row. A verified address that is not an active directory user gets 401 and no proof. This is DGO_OTP_VERIFY's mint (retired 2026-10-06), placed in the live flow.
- Set variable values held in a Compose step (the designer dropped inline and changed Set variable values on paste; tenant export of IP_Create__Task__for_received_Email_Endpoint, 6 October 2026): Set_variable_Verification_Not_A_Directory_User, Set_variable_varData.
- ITEM-82: Case_Generate leaves IP_OTP_VERIFY. Owner decision 2026-10-07: generation and verification run on separate flows; a Folio sign-in on 2026-10-08 ran generation in IP_OTP_GENERATE (05:14:59Z) and verification here (05:16:15Z, proof created), so this flow now only verifies. A generate request answers 400 from the Switch default.
- The sign-in proof is redacted from the run record (tenant defect, 8 October 2026): Compose_Redacted_Headers masked Authorization but not X-DGO-Proof, where the proof travels since release 9, so every telemetry row held a usable session token.

Steps added: `Get_Otp_Directory_User`, `Compose_Otp_Proof_Token`, `Compose_Otp_Proof_Expires`, `Condition_Otp_Known_User`, `Create_Otp_Proof`, `Set_variable_Verification_Not_A_Directory_User`, `Append_to_string_variable_Verification_Not_A_Directory_User`, `Compose_Value_Set_variable_Verification_Not_A_Directory_User`, `Condition_Otp_Has_Pending_Code`, `Compose_Value_Set_variable_varData`.

Steps removed: `Compose_OTP_Expiry`, `Create_item_OTP_Record`, `Append_to_string_variable_varResponse_Generate_OTP`, `Set_variable_varStatusCode_Generate_OTP`, `Send_an_email_(V2)`.

**How to apply.** Paste over Scope_Global in IP_OTP_VERIFY (4dbe6dde), the one flow OTP_GENERATE and OTP_VERIFY run on. The proof ledger (Global_Digital_Documents_Centre, f5c9698e) already exists. Set Flow Configuration IDENTITY_PROOF_REQUIRED to true only after a sign-in has returned a proof.

**Test after pasting.** Sign in to Folio with an emailed code as an active directory user. The reply's data carries token, expiresAt (four hours ahead) and claims with the directory row's role; the proof ledger has a row with that token as Title, Purpose internal-session, Consumed No and the same expiry; the next Folio call sends Authorization: Bearer <token>. Sign in with a correct code as an address that is not in DGO_UserDirectory: 401 NOT_A_DIRECTORY_USER and no ledger row.

### OTP_GENERATE

- Owner decision, 2026-10-07: OTP_GENERATE has a flow of its own. This is the OTP_VERIFY package with Case_Verify removed: the code is created in OTP_Transactions and e-mailed exactly as IP_OTP_VERIFY does it; a verify request answers 400 from the Switch default.
- Codes go only to active directory users: Case_Generate looks the address up in DGO_UserDirectory (active rows) and creates and mails the code only when it is found. The reply (200, OTP sent, the expiry) is the same for any address, so the endpoint does not reveal who is a user; IP_OTP_VERIFY still refuses a proof to anyone outside the directory.
- The sign-in proof is redacted from the run record (tenant defect, 8 October 2026): Compose_Redacted_Headers masked Authorization but not X-DGO-Proof, where the proof travels since release 9, so every telemetry row held a usable session token.
- ITEM-66: every mail send writes a receipt to Portal Outbox Receipts (Send_an_email_(V2)): message type, recipient (the send's own To), the run as reference, sent or failed, and the error on failure; never the message body. Compose_<send>_Outcome fails exactly when the send failed, so the scope around it ends as it did before the receipt was added and the flow's catch path still fires.

The scope is new: it replaces the flow's Scope_Global as a whole (29 steps).

**How to apply.** Created in the tenant by the Flow API (2026-10-07). Point Folio's OTP_GENERATE URL at this flow; once a sign-in has run through it, Case_Generate leaves IP_OTP_VERIFY.

**Test after pasting.** Sign in to Folio: the code arrives from dgsregistry@nitda.gov.ng, and the run appears in IP_OTP_GENERATE's history (not IP_OTP_VERIFY's); OTP_Transactions has the new row; Portal Outbox Receipts has a row with Status sent. Entering the code verifies through IP_OTP_VERIFY as before.

### REFERENCE_DATA

- S8 / ID-19: the run sets its own Request ID (varRequestId = guid()) first. The flow declared it from the client's correlation id or requestId when one was sent.
- G-04: the caller is resolved as every identification package resolves it (see "Caller identity" above): from the sign-in proof when one is valid; else, while IDENTITY_PROOF_REQUIRED is not true, from userEmail as today. The role is read from the directory row's Role choice, which the flow read as text and so never matched a RoleId.
- A caller with no role-permission row made the read fail with 500: Compose_Lookups_Permissions_Array and Compose_Lookups_Routes_Array chose between json('[]') and json(<the row's text>) with if(), which evaluates both, and json('') throws. They now parse one string, '[]' when the row is absent or empty. With the switch true this is what lets a caller with no proof be answered 401 rather than 500.
- The reference data endpoint answered anyone: Condition_Lookups_Authorised read Compose_temp_fix_permtted and Compose_temp_fix_caller, which hold the literal true, in place of the caller and permission check the flow computes. Those steps (and Compose_actual_expressions_Condition_Lookups_Authorised, which only displayed the real values) are removed, and the condition decides on the caller: while IDENTITY_PROOF_REQUIRED is not true it passes as today; when it is true, the caller must be an active DGO_UserDirectory user resolved from a valid proof, else 401 UNAUTHENTICATED. The role's route and permission (Compose_Lookups_Permitted) are still not enforced: which roles hold them is not recorded in this repository, and enforcing them unverified would lock officers out.
- Directory and reference data as Folio reads them, as FETCH_ALL's package reads them (ported from the retired DGO_REFERENCE_DATA design, registers/flow-retirement.json): the directory is read in pages to 5,000 rows (it holds 852; the flow read one page of 500), Role, Persona and Status are served as text rather than Choice objects, and Departments and Categories, imported from spreadsheets so GetItems returns field_1…field_N, are read by those internal names. The keys Folio reads are unchanged.
- The full directory only to a holder of user:view (or of every route, "*"), as the retired DGO_REFERENCE_DATA design served it. Every caller gets every active user's UserId, FullName, Email, Directorate and Department, which the Workspace needs to address and assign; Role, Persona, Status, AccessScope and PilotCohort are served for the caller's own row and, to anyone else, as null. The rows and their keys are unchanged; one Select does it, so no Filter array is pasted.
- ITEM-52: the Response_Lookups run record carries the reply's size instead of the reply, and the read endpoint no longer e-mails its run record (owner decision 2026-10-06; tenant evidence 2026-10-10).
- Set variable values held in a Compose step (the designer dropped inline and changed Set variable values on paste; tenant export of IP_Create__Task__for_received_Email_Endpoint, 6 October 2026): Set_Lookups_Catch_Data, Set_Lookups_Denied_Data, Set_Lookups_Denied_Status, Set_Lookups_Success_Data, Set_variable_varRequestId.
- The sign-in proof is redacted from the run record (tenant defect, 8 October 2026): Compose_Redacted_Headers masked Authorization but not X-DGO-Proof, where the proof travels since release 9, so every telemetry row held a usable session token.

Steps added: `Compose_Lookups_Sees_Directory`, `Compose_Value_Set_Lookups_Success_Data`, `Compose_Value_Set_Lookups_Denied_Data`, `Compose_Value_Set_Lookups_Denied_Status`, `Get_Lookups_Gate_Proof_Mode`, `Compose_Lookups_Gate_Proof_Token`, `Get_Lookups_Gate_Proof`, `Compose_Lookups_Gate_Identity`, `Compose_Lookups_Gate_Caller`, `Compose_Value_Set_Lookups_Catch_Data`, `Set_variable_varRequestId`, `Compose_Value_Set_variable_varRequestId`.

Steps removed: `Compose_temp_fix_permtted`, `Compose_temp_fix_caller`, `Compose_actual_expressions_Condition_Lookups_Authorised`, `Compose_Telemetry_Attachments`, `Send_Telemetry_Email`.

**How to apply.** Paste over Scope_Global in IP_Reference_Data_Endpoint (9a4dea8e). SharePoint connections arrive bound. Paste before IDENTITY_PROOF_REQUIRED is set to true.

**Test after pasting.** Open Folio as an officer whose role holds user:view: the directory lists every active user (more than 500 if the directory holds them) with Role, Persona and Status as text, and the category and department pickers show codes and heads. Open it as an officer whose role does not: every user is listed with name, e-mail, directorate and department, Role and the rest are blank except on the officer's own row. With IDENTITY_PROOF_REQUIRED true, call REFERENCE_DATA with no Authorization header: 401 UNAUTHENTICATED.

### FETCH_EMAIL_ATTACHMENTS

- G-04: the endpoint had no caller check at all: anyone holding its URL could read the attachments of any message in the mailbox by its id. It now resolves the caller from the sign-in proof (else, while IDENTITY_PROOF_REQUIRED is not true, from userEmail) and looks the caller up in DGO_UserDirectory. While the switch is not true it answers as today; when it is true, a caller who is not an active directory user resolved from a valid proof gets 401 UNAUTHENTICATED and no message is read. The steps are SharePoint reads, so the flow gains a SharePoint connection (the one the other endpoint flows use).
- Set variable values held in a Compose step (the designer dropped inline and changed Set variable values on paste; tenant export of IP_Create__Task__for_received_Email_Endpoint, 6 October 2026): Set_Catch_Data, Set_Invalid_Data, Set_Invalid_Outcome, Set_Invalid_Status, Set_Success_Data.

### EMAIL

- S8 / ID-19: the run sets its own Request ID (varRequestId = guid()) first. The flow declared it from the client's correlation id or requestId when one was sent.
- G-04: the caller is resolved from the sign-in proof when one is valid; else, while IDENTITY_PROOF_REQUIRED is not true, from userEmail as today. The flow's own directory check then decides: with the switch true and no valid proof the caller is nobody, no directory row matches, and Condition_SendEmail_Known_Caller answers 401 UNAUTHENTICATED; nothing is sent.
- F1 (e-mail template package, ITEM-92): Compose_SendEmail_Hero_Schemes holds the package's hero schemes; Compose_SendEmail_Hero picks the one payload.email.hero.purpose names (else the frame's own colours) and carries the chip, title, lead and footer note the frame prints.
- Set variable values held in a Compose step (the designer dropped inline and changed Set variable values on paste; tenant export of IP_Create__Task__for_received_Email_Endpoint, 6 October 2026): Set_variable_varData_SendEmail_Attached, Set_variable_varData_SendEmail_Catch, Set_variable_varData_SendEmail_Denied_401, Set_variable_varData_SendEmail_Duplicate, Set_variable_varData_SendEmail_Invalid, Set_variable_varData_SendEmail_Plain, Set_variable_varRequestId.
- The sign-in proof is redacted from the run record (tenant defect, 8 October 2026): Compose_Redacted_Headers masked Authorization but not X-DGO-Proof, where the proof travels since release 9, so every telemetry row held a usable session token.

Steps added: `Compose_Value_Set_variable_varData_SendEmail_Attached`, `Compose_Value_Set_variable_varData_SendEmail_Plain`, `Compose_Value_Set_variable_varData_SendEmail_Duplicate`, `Compose_Value_Set_variable_varData_SendEmail_Invalid`, `Compose_SendEmail_Hero_Schemes`, `Compose_SendEmail_Hero`, `Compose_Value_Set_variable_varData_SendEmail_Denied_401`, `Get_SendEmail_Gate_Proof_Mode`, `Compose_SendEmail_Gate_Proof_Token`, `Get_SendEmail_Gate_Proof`, `Compose_SendEmail_Gate_Identity`, `Compose_SendEmail_Gate_Caller`, `Compose_Value_Set_variable_varData_SendEmail_Catch`, `Set_variable_varRequestId`, `Compose_Value_Set_variable_varRequestId`.

### AI

- G-04: AI_Document_Processing (AI_EMAIL_ANALYSIS, AI_DOC_ANALYSIS, AI_CHAT) had no caller check: it read any DGO DIGITAL OPS item's attachments and sent them to an external model for anyone holding its URL. Its steps sit at the top level of the flow, so this is an added scope, not a replacement: it resolves the caller from the sign-in proof (else, while IDENTITY_PROOF_REQUIRED is not true, from userEmail) and looks the caller up in DGO_UserDirectory. While the switch is not true it does nothing visible; when it is true, a caller who is not an active directory user resolved from a valid proof gets 401 UNAUTHENTICATED and the run stops before any item is read.
- Security (ITEM-75): the flow's HTTP action sends an OpenRouter key as literal text in its Authorization header, so every copy of the definition carries it. This scope reads the key from Flow Configuration (OPENROUTER_API_KEY) and composes the header value, Compose_OpenRouter_Authorization = "Bearer <key>". After pasting, set the HTTP action's Authorization header to @{outputs('Compose_OpenRouter_Authorization')}: that one field is the only edit outside this scope, and afterwards the definition holds no key. With no row the value is "Bearer " and the AI call is refused by OpenRouter rather than sent with the old key.

The scope is new: it replaces the flow's Scope_AI_Caller_Gate as a whole (12 steps).

**How to apply.** First add a Flow Configuration row OPENROUTER_API_KEY holding a new OpenRouter key (ITEM-75). This scope is added, not replaced: in AI_Document_Processing (fefa43c6) select the + between Initialize_variable_2 and Get_item, choose Paste an action, paste the file. Then open the HTTP action and set its Authorization header to @{outputs('Compose_OpenRouter_Authorization')}, replacing the key text. Save, then revoke the old key in OpenRouter.

**Test after pasting.** Run an AI analysis from Folio signed in: it answers as before, and in the run history the HTTP action's Authorization shows the configured key, while Export (or Peek code on HTTP) shows only the expression. With IDENTITY_PROOF_REQUIRED true, call AI_DOC_ANALYSIS with no Authorization header: 401 UNAUTHENTICATED, and the run is Cancelled at Terminate_AI_Gate with Get_item not run.

### SCAN_PROCESSING

- Trigger: the OneDrive trigger reports a file's properties, not its content (When a file is created (properties only), split per file). Get_Trigger_Document_Content reads the content first, and every reference to the old trigger reads the new one: the content from Get_Trigger_Document_Content, the file id and name from the trigger's Id and Name, the folder from its Path.
- One account: the legacy flow spread its work over three OneDrive and two SharePoint connections, some signed in as other people. Every OneDrive step uses the flow's own OneDrive connection (dgsRegistry@nitda.gov.ng) and every SharePoint step the registry's SharePoint connection (3f1943c5).
- No copy to another person's OneDrive: the legacy flow copied each document to "/2024 DOCUMENTS/Documente Volume II" in a second account and renamed that copy. The document stays where it arrived and is renamed there (Rename_Trigger_File*); CREATE_COPY_OF_TRIGGER_DOCUMENT becomes Get_Trigger_Document_Metadata, which reads the same Id, Name and DisplayName of the file itself, and the steps that moved the copy are removed.
- No flow definition by e-mail: Scope_Flow_Definition_Email read the flow's own definition and mailed it on every run (ITEM-52's surplus pattern). It is removed with its Flow management connection; nothing else read it.
- Deep links: APP_FAST_TRACK_LINK points at the internal platform, not the retired Power Apps player, and Set_variable_Deeplink / Set_variable_Deeplink_2 lose the stray "veggie " suffix the legacy flow appended to every link (the fix npm run deeplinks:patches gave for the legacy flow).
- Security: the flow held three Google AI API keys as literal text (Compose_API_Key, Compose_API_Key_2 and Compose_API_Key_kanihamza@gmail.com__v2), so every copy of its definition carried them, this repository's capture included. They are now read from Flow Configuration: GEMINI_API_KEY, and GEMINI_API_KEY_2 for the second key the text extraction uses (GEMINI_API_KEY when that row is absent). The step names are unchanged, so the AI calls that read them need no change. The keys that were in the definition are exposed and are to be revoked in Google Cloud and replaced (readiness register).
- Placement: the flow's six variable declarations stay at the top level (Initialise_All_Text_Variable, Initialize_variable_Key_Points, Initialize_variableDeepLink, Initialize_variable_Document_Link, Initialise_varResponse, Initialize_variable_New_File_Name); the rest of the legacy flow is one scope, Scope_Scan_Processing, which starts by reading the document's content.
- S7 / §8.2: every document the library intake takes in becomes a registered record, as a portal submission or a scan does. After the DGO DIGITAL OPS row is created, the scope claims the next NITDA-YYYY-NNNNN (the kit claim, floored at the register's highest number) and writes the Portal Registry row: Title and ReferenceId, Subject the file name, Channel library, CorrespondenceType Incoming, SenderEmail the registry mailbox (Flow Configuration NOTIFY_REGISTRY_TO, else dgsregistry@nitda.gov.ng, as for scans), Status received, AttachmentCount 1, EntityKey, IdState ACTIVE, Rev 1, Direction In, CorrelationId and CreatedByRequest, and SourceLocator spo:<DGO DIGITAL OPS>/<item ID>.
- §10.2 OPS_WORKING_REGISTER: the DGO DIGITAL OPS row gets the record's EntityKey, ReferenceId and IdState ACTIVE by the kit's Guarded Update (IF-MATCH; the list has no Rev column). DGO_IdentityMap gets the row as the record's SPO_ITEM locator: Container the DGO DIGITAL OPS list, Value the item ID, MatchKey LOCATOR|SPO_ITEM|<list>|<ID>. If the register row cannot be written, a VOID row accounts for the number (Q2) and the DGO DIGITAL OPS row is left without a key. If no number can be claimed, nothing is written. Either way the scope ends Succeeded, so the AI processing that follows runs as before.
- S7 / §8.2: Scope_Library_Identity (the registry record, its NITDA-YYYY-NNNNN and its DGO_IdentityMap locator, as designed for the legacy flow) runs after Preliminaries_and_Backup has created the DGO DIGITAL OPS row; Scope_Processing runs after it, whatever it ends.
- B5 (e-mail template package, ITEM-92): removed 5 unread steps that load images from third-party hosts (Compose_Email_Notification_with_AI_Processed_Information_version_1, Compose_Email_Notification_with_AI_Processed_Information_version_2, Compose_4, Compose_5, Compose_Email_Attachments_3); nothing reads them, and the steps that ran after them run after their predecessors.
- ITEM-66: every mail send writes a receipt to Portal Outbox Receipts (Send_an_email_(V2)): message type, recipient (the send's own To), the run as reference, sent or failed, and the error on failure; never the message body. Compose_<send>_Outcome fails exactly when the send failed, so the scope around it ends as it did before the receipt was added and the flow's catch path still fires.

The scope is new: it replaces the flow's Scope_Scan_Processing as a whole (212 steps).

**How to apply.** Written whole by scripts/write-scan-processing-flow.mjs (trigger on the OneDrive folder /E-DOCUMENT STATION, bound to the OneDrive connection that reaches it, the six variable declarations, this scope), then kept current by npm run flows:update.

**Test after pasting.** Scan a document to /E-DOCUMENT STATION. Within a minute: DGO DIGITAL OPS has a new row with the file name, the extracted text in Notes and the AI summary in Description, the document attached and renamed "<ID> -<date> -<name>"; Portal Registry has a row with Channel library and the next NITDA-YYYY-NNNNN; dgs@nitda.gov.ng receives "New E-Scan"; Portal Outbox Receipts records it.

### SWEEP

- Owner direction 2026-10-10: one e-mail per person, not one per task. The acknowledgement-overdue and task-overdue loops are replaced by a digest: the eligible tasks of both (the same rules: not acknowledged or not completed, a single valid address) are gathered, and each person receives one e-mail listing all their items, at most once a day (a receipt task-digest:<address>:<date> is written and checked). Until Flow Configuration NOTIFY_SWEEP_RECIPIENTS is staff, every digest goes to the registry (NOTIFY_OPS_TO) with the intended person named, and the closed-support-case notices go there too: nobody outside the registry is written to before commissioning. The working-hours and NOTIFY_ENABLED switches still apply.
- Tenant defect 2026-10-18 (AUTO_SCHEDULED_SWEEP run 08584093115454153780858604181CU30): a SharePoint date-only column comes back without a zone, and convertFromUtc refused it. Every date this package converts from a list row, a trigger body or a connector reply (5) is read with a Z added when it has none, and an empty one reads as the epoch.
- ITEM-66: every mail send writes a receipt to Portal Outbox Receipts (Send_Case_Email, Send_Undeliverable_Alert_Email, Send_Task_Reminder_Email, Send_Server_Error_Alert_Email): message type, recipient (the send's own To), the run as reference, sent or failed, and the error on failure; never the message body. Compose_<send>_Outcome fails exactly when the send failed, so the scope around it ends as it did before the receipt was added and the flow's catch path still fires.

The scope is new: it replaces the flow's Scope_ScheduledSweep_Flow as a whole (103 steps).

**How to apply.** Written by npm run flows:update (the flow is Stopped). Its schedule is set to weekdays at 08:45 WAT by a separate trigger write. Start it only at commissioning, and set Flow Configuration NOTIFY_SWEEP_RECIPIENTS to staff only when staff may receive the digests.

**Test after pasting.** Run the sweep once by hand while NOTIFY_SWEEP_RECIPIENTS is not staff: the registry receives one e-mail per person with overdue or unacknowledged tasks, each naming that person and listing all their tasks; Portal Outbox Receipts has one task-digest:<address>:<date> row per person. Run it again the same day: nothing is sent.

### FAILURE_WATCH

- Owner decision 2026-10-18: every failed notice is registered; only some are reported. The watch reads Flow Configuration (NOTIFY_FAILURE_WATCH_ENABLED, NOTIFY_FAILURE_REPORT_GROUPS, NOTIFY_FAILURE_BURST, NOTIFY_FAILURE_REPORT_TO, and the cursor and health rows it writes itself), falling back to config/notification-failure-groups.config.js when a row is absent.
- The window: failures registered after the cursor and up to this run's start (Created), so each is read by exactly one run; a run that cannot read leaves the cursor, and the next run reads the window again. Then every failure still open (Status failed), for the counts and the 07:00 summary. Each failure is placed by its receipt's MessageType, or by flow and type where two flows share a type. Only the reference, type, masked recipient, error and time are carried: never a message body.
- What is reported: in the 07:00 run, every reportable failure still open (the morning summary); in every other run, the reportable failures registered since the last run, each once. Reportable: the groups in NOTIFY_FAILURE_REPORT_GROUPS (default citizen, unclassified), and any failure the mapping cannot place. A burst (NOTIFY_FAILURE_BURST or more failures of any group in the window, default 5) is reported as a broken mail connection. Nothing is sent when there is nothing to report, or when NOTIFY_FAILURE_WATCH_ENABLED is false.
- Afterwards: the cursor moves to this run's start only when the window was read, and NOTIFY_FAILURE_HEALTH is written (the open count per group, the burst flag, the time) only when the open failures were read. Each row is created on the first run if it is absent.
- ITEM-66: every mail send writes a receipt to Portal Outbox Receipts (Send_Failure_Watch_Email): message type, recipient (the send's own To), the run as reference, sent or failed, and the error on failure; never the message body. Compose_<send>_Outcome fails exactly when the send failed, so the scope around it ends as it did before the receipt was added and the flow's catch path still fires.

The scope is new: it replaces the flow's Scope_Failure_Watch as a whole (34 steps).

**How to apply.** Created by scripts/write-failure-watch-flow.mjs (a Recurrence trigger: every hour, Monday to Friday, 07:00 to 18:00 WAT; this scope), then kept current by npm run flows:update. Record its id in scripts/lib/flow-artifact-name.mjs FLOW_IDENTITIES and capture it.

**Test after pasting.** Make one notice fail on purpose in each group (a citizen outcome to an address that does not exist, a staff notice, a sign-in code). Each has a Portal Outbox Receipts row with Status failed. At the next hour the registry receives one Folio Failure Watch e-mail listing only the citizen outcome; the next run does not list it again; the 07:00 run lists it while its Status is failed. Five failures in one hour bring the broken-connection line. Flow Configuration NOTIFY_FAILURE_HEALTH holds the open count per group, and the Workspace's System Health shows it.
